RootCause.Observed: StartWithWindows remained true in application configuration and Windows StartupApproved was enabled, but the HKCU Run value for TaskbarMonitorEnhanced was absent after the power-loss/restart event. The protected sensor supervisor still launched from its separate logon task.
RootCause.FailureMode: The v1.1.2 main application could repair its Run value only after it was already running, so loss of the only main-app launch registration created a bootstrap gap.

Fix.Recovery: Current-user Startup-folder shortcut: Taskbar Monitor Enhanced Startup Recovery.lnk
Fix.RepairRule: Either surviving startup path launches the application and the application recreates the missing registration.
Fix.DuplicateProtection: Recovery exits early when a primary process is present; existing named mutex remains final single-instance guard.
Fix.PrivilegeModel: Per-user only; no administrator privilege is required for the two startup registrations.

SensorLayer.Rationale: v1.1.3 is an app/startup reliability patch and preserves the accepted protected sensor layer.

StartupFaultInjection.Test: Missing HKCU Run with recovery shortcut surviving
StartupFaultInjection.Evidence: Recovery path launched; after its bounded wait the main app recreated the exact Run value; exactly one main process remained.

StartupFaultInjection.Test: Missing recovery shortcut with HKCU Run surviving
StartupFaultInjection.Evidence: Normal launch recreated the recovery shortcut with the exact installed target and --startup-recovery argument; exactly one main process remained.

StartupFaultInjection.Test: Recovery launch while primary already running
StartupFaultInjection.Evidence: Fallback exited with code 0 within the bounded observation window; original primary PID remained the sole main process.
Both Run and recovery shortcut were absent while the app remained usable; original user setting was then restored and both registrations returned.
